sentence: A group-privacy approach for personalized FL using d-privacy over Euclidean distance reports FEMNIST accuracy of 0.835 at noise multiplier ν = 3 — slightly *above* the 0.832 at ν = 0 — with accuracy collapsing to 0.692 at ν = 10 and 0.561 at ν = 15, and a gradient-inversion attack failing for ν ≥ 1 [cited].
ref: F Galli, et al. Group privacy for personalized federated learning. arXiv preprint, 2022. https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.03396

sentence: The obvious weakness is that the dropout rate is a hyperparameter, which is what Concrete dropout removes: a continuous (Gumbel-softmax) relaxation makes the per-layer dropout probability differentiable so it can be learned, recovering hand-tuned performance without the search (CamVid/DenseNet IoU 67.4 versus 67.2 for hand-tuned p=0.2) and revealing that the optimal rate shrinks toward zero in early layers and grows with depth and model size [cited].
ref: Y. Gal, Jiri Hron, Alex Kendall. Concrete dropout. NIPS, 2017. https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2017/hash/84ddfb34126fc3a48ee38d7044e87276-Abstract.html

ref: W Fei, et al. Retrieval meets reasoning: Dynamic in-context editing for long-text understanding. arXiv preprint, 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12331

sentence: Thought-Retriever [[cited]] makes a different structural bet — store distilled *thoughts* (validated, deduplicated answer-level abstractions) rather than raw chunks, then retrieve over thoughts and chunks jointly — reporting at least 7.6% F1 and 16% win-rate gains, beating a gold-chunk oracle on its own AcademicEval benchmark, running >25× faster than MemWalker, and showing held-out self-evolution of +6.4% as the thought memory grows.
ref: T Feng, et al. Thought-Retriever: Don't Just Retrieve Raw Data, Retrieve Thoughts for Memory-Augmented Agentic Systems. arXiv preprint, 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12231

sentence: DASH built a PEM single cell and ran it for 125 hours [cited].

sentence: And using LLM agents to *simulate* users is a genuinely different proposition with a genuinely different validation standard: RecAgent builds agents with profiles, a three-tier memory model and six action types, and validates them against real humans rather than against a downstream metric — 68% above the best baseline but 8% below real humans on item-overlap, with a 45.0% vs 33.3% adversarial win rate against RecSim [cited].
ref: Lei Wang, et al. User Behavior Simulation with Large Language Model-based Agents. ACM Trans. Inf. Syst., 2024. https://doi.org/10.1145/3708985

sentence: The strongest empirical answer comes from Geom3D, a benchmark spanning 16 geometric models, 10 2D GNNs, 7 1D baselines, 14 pretraining algorithms and 52 tasks across small molecules, proteins, crystals and binding [cited].
ref: S Liu, et al. Symmetry-informed geometric representation for molecules, proteins, and crystalline materials. 2023. https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/d07379f3acf3af51dfc8598862cadfa0-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks.html

sentence: CRITIC, which routes critiques through a search engine, a code interpreter and a toxicity API, gains 7.7 F1 across three QA sets, 7.0% on math, and a 79.2% reduction in toxicity probability — and the ablations show the tools carry the effect, since removing them collapses the gains [cited].
ref: Z Gou, et al. Critic: Large language models can self-correct with tool-interactive critiquing. 2024. https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/fef126561bbf9d4467dbb8d27334b8fe-Abstract-Conference.html

sentence: AlphaProteo reports the strongest binder numbers to date — 9–88% success on 7 of 8 targets, best K_D 82 pM, without high-throughput screening — but it also failed completely on TNFα, a flat and highly polar interface, and three of its targets were used during method development [cited].
ref: Vinicius Zambaldi, et al. De novo design of high-affinity protein binders with AlphaProteo. arXiv (Cornell University), 2024. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2409.08022

sentence: Two things about the evidence deserve emphasis: it is synthetic only (dz=10, dx=20, 1M examples), and the paper's most quotable empirical result is a *negative* one about baselines — they achieve high R² but low MCC, meaning they are linearly identifiable without being disentangled [cited].
ref: Sébastien Lachapelle, et al. Disentanglement via Mechanism Sparsity Regularization: A New Principle for Nonlinear ICA. CLeaR, 2021. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v177/lachapelle22a.html

sentence: Cascading Instruction Influence [cited] models injection propagating through three-tier delegation chains, validated statistically against behavioural data from ten production LLMs, and reports a large effect for hierarchical versus centralised topologies (Cohen's d = 2.34, 95% CI 1.82–2.86) — the argument being that hierarchy depth *raises* risk rather than containing it.
ref: MRM Abdellah, AS Aziz. Cascading Instruction Influence Indirect Prompt Injection in Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems. 2026. https://iapress.org/index.php/soic/article/view/3574

sentence: AlphaProteo designs high-affinity protein binders with 3- to 300-fold better binding affinities and higher experimental success rates than prior methods [cited].
ref: Vinicius Zambaldi, David La, Alexander E. Chu, et al. De novo design of high-affinity protein binders with AlphaProteo. arXiv (Cornell University), 2024. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2409.08022
